comparator.route: Strategy and Organisation (Strategie en Organisatie) specialisation
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted programme chart gives 60 compulsory EC in year one (ten 6-EC modules); 48 compulsory EC and two separate 6-EC restricted choices in year two (the first-listed Accounting II in period four, Entrepreneurship in period five); and a third year with 30 EC genuinely open minor space, 6 EC Ethics, two 6-EC courses in one formally selected specialisation, and a 12-EC thesis tied to that specialisation. The Strategy and Organisation specialisation has Foundations of Strategic Management and Strategic Management from a Practice Perspective. It is selected as the most general business-management specialisation, independently of UCR fit; more narrowly functional routes such as Accounting, Finance and Marketing are not mixed in. Zero-credit research participation and personal/professional-development items are not added to the 180 EC. No optional alternative choice is presented as compulsory for all students.

comparatorRouteSelection.route: Strategy and Organisation (Strategie en Organisatie) specialisation
comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic normalized Bedrijfskunde target requires one of the formally listed year-three specialisations to be instantiated. Strategy and Organisation is the broadest management/organisational strategy direction rather than a narrow functional area; the two named 6-EC units and linked 12-EC thesis are taken together from annex VII of the adopted 2026–27 OER. This academic representation was chosen before comparing UCR courses.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The first curriculum covers broad business functions, the second adds technical digital-business and AI work, and the third concentrates on organisational change and people. All three concepts follow target-specific interests, produce materially different 24-course selections, and meet the pairwise four-course floor. Transport/supply-chain management is a separate supported interest but UCR has no dedicated logistics sequence to support a further 24-course direction; in any event three defensible options already meet the maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both cultivate academic research and communication skills, with UCR covering broader personal and professional development.
Both examine legal constraints on businesses, but UCR emphasises cross-border commercial law.
Both deal with entrepreneurship and organising new ventures; UCR gives the broader foundational account.
Both address managing people and organisational behaviour; UCR focuses on diverse teams and leadership.
Both investigate how organisations function and how managers influence people; UCR emphasizes organisational psychology.
Both use qualitative inquiry; UCR applies it across social research rather than only organisations.

notes.text: VU combines prescribed business functions and methods with a third-year Strategy and Organisation specialisation, a 12-EC thesis and a 30-EC open minor. UCR offers business, economics, leadership, research and digital courses in more flexible combinations, without reproducing the VU supply-chain sequence, advanced accounting choice or specialisation thesis.
